newsitem.title: INDIA: Depositors protest as India finance firm goes bust.
newsitem.headline: Depositors protest as India finance firm goes bust.

text.p: Angry depositors demonstrated outside the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for the second day on Saturday after the central bank began winding-up proceedings against a finance firm.
A New Delhi court appointed a provisional liquidator on Thursday and restrained the crippled CRB Capital Markets from disposing of its assets after the RBI filed a petition seeking its liquidation.
Saddled with high-cost funds and falling interest rates the firm was unable to repay depositors when they demanded their money back, officials said.

Finance firms offered interest rates of up to 22 percent on deposits to overcome a severe liquidity crunch two years ago. Lending rates have since tumbled to between 14 and 16 percent after the central bank loosened purse strings.
The company's exact liabilities are not known but newspapers have estimated it at between three billion rupees and six billion against assets of about 1.33 billion.
Some depositors blamed the RBI for not monitoring finance firms more closely, while others said they were fooled by deposit agents.
"The agents are more to blame than anyone else," said Arvind Chitnis, who had fixed deposits worth 96,000 rupees with CRB.

"I believe they were getting a hefty commission from the company to attract depositors. Naturally they painted a rosy picture which lured innocent investors into placing money with the company," he said.
Another depositor said he had been carried away by the firm's brochures and prospectus.
R.R Mayekar, a retired man, invested 5,000 rupees based on promises of lucrative returns made by the firm's brochures.
A banker said finance firms were hit by shrinking merchant banking activities after a two-year long stock market slump.
